label: lemma:clopen-normalizers
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:clopen-normalizers}
    
     Let $X$ be a zero-dimensional, compact, Hausdorff space, and $A$ a \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra containing $C(X)$. The set $N_{A}^{c}(C(X))$ is dense in $N_{A}(C(X))$. Moreover, any $a\in N_A^c(C(X))$ has a polar decomposition $a=v\left|a\right|$ in $A$, with $\left|a\right|\in C(X)$ and $v\in N_A^c(C(X))$ a partial isometry for which $v^*v=\mathbbm{1}_{\operatorname{supp}(a)}$ and $vv^*=\mathbbm{1}_{\operatorname{ran}(a)}$.

label: lemma:npi_extends
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:npi_extends}
    Let $A$ be \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra with a faithful trace $\tau$ and containing $C(X)$, with $X$ a zero-dimensional, compact, Hausdorff space. Write $\mathcal{M} := \pi_\tau(A)''$ and write $ L^{\infty}(X,\mu_\tau):=\pi_\tau(C(X))''\subseteq \mathcal{M} $ with $\pi_\tau$ the GNS representation associated to $\tau$ and $\mu_\tau$ the measure on $X$ induced by $\tau$. For any $v\in N_A(C(X))$, there exists a unitary $u\in N_{\mathcal{M}}(L^{\infty}(X,\mu_\tau))$ such that $vv^{*}uv^{*}v=v$.

label: lemma:no-atoms-in-vna
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first show that $A$ is either atomic or diffuse. Arguing by contradiction, we suppose that $A$ is neither so that $A=L^\infty(X)\oplus \ell^\infty(Y)$ for a diffuse measure space $X$ and a non-empty, countable set $Y$.
    Denote by $p=1_{L^\infty(X)}$ the unit of $L^\infty(X)$.
    Then there is a nonzero partial isometry $v\in N_\mathcal{M}(A) \cap p \mathcal{M}(1-p)$, as otherwise $N_{\mathcal{M}}(A)$ would be contained in the proper von Neumann subalgebra $p\mathcal{M} p\oplus (1-p)\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}} (1-p)$ of $\mathcal{M}$, contradicting regularity of $A$.
    Let 
    \begin{equation}
        T:=\left\{ \tau(p) : p\in \ell^\infty(Y)\text{ is a projection} \right\}, 
    \end{equation}
    which is a countable set.
    Fix $s \in \mathbb{R}\setminus T$ such that $0<s< \tau(vv^*)$ and find $q\in L^\infty(X)$ such that $\tau(q)=s$ and $q\leq vv^*$.
    Then $v^*qv\leq 1-p$ is a projection of trace $\tau(v^*qv) = \tau(q) =s$ which, since $v$ normalizes $A$, satisfies
    \begin{equation} 
    v^*qv\in A \cap (1-p)\mathcal{M}(1-p) = \ell^\infty(Y).
    \end{equation}
    This contradicts the definition of $T$ and so $A$ is either diffuse or atomic.

    Now suppose that $A$ is atomic, and let $P$ be the (countable) set of minimal projections in $A$.
    Consider the action $\alpha: U(N_{\mathcal{M}}(A))\curvearrowright P$ by unitary conjugation. As $P$ is countable, $\alpha$ is a permutation of $P$.
    Let $S\subseteq P$ be an arbitrary $\alpha$-invariant subset of $P$.
    Then for all $u\in U(N_{\mathcal{M}}(A))$, $\alpha(u)$ fixes $S$, so $u$ commutes with the indicator function $\ensuremath{\mathbbm{1}}_{S}$ of $S$.
    By regularity of $A$ and the fact that unitary normalizers also generate $\mathcal{M}$ in this case by \cite[Lemma~12.1.2]{Delaroche-Popa}, it follows that $\ensuremath{\mathbbm{1}} _S$ is central in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}} $ and thus either 0 or 1.
    Consequently, the action $\alpha$ is transitive on $P$ and since it is furthermore trace-preserving, $\tau(p)=\tau(q)$ for all $p,q\in P$.
    Hence $P$ must be finite and so $A$ is finite-dimensional.

label: cor:diffuse
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:diffuse}
    Let $B$ be a simple $C^*$-algebra containing $C(X)$ as a regular $C^*$-subalgebra, with $X$ an infinite, compact Hausdorff space. Any trace $\tau$ on $B$ is diffuse on $C(X)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: As $B$ contains $C(X)$ as a regular $C^*$-subalgebra, it follows that $\mathcal{M} := \pi_\tau(B)''$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor containing $L^\infty(X,\mu_{\tau})$ as a regular von Neumann subalgebra, with $\pi_\tau$ the GNS representation of $B$ associated to $\tau$ and $\mu_\tau$ the measure on $X$ induced by $\tau$. From the previous lemma, it then follows that $L^\infty(X,\mu_{\tau})$ is either finite-dimensional or diffuse. However, it cannot be finite-dimensional, as $\tau$ is faithful and $X$ is infinite. This concludes the proof.

title: Definition
body_md:
A unital \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra is said to be \emph{tracially approximately finite dimensional} (tracially AF) if for any non-empty finite subset $\mathcal{F} \subset A$ with  $x_1$, any $\varepsilon > 0$ and any $a \in A_+$, there exists a finite dimensional \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra $B \subset A$ with $p=1_B$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item $px \approx_\varepsilon xp$ for all $x \in \mathfrak{F}$,
        \item $\mathrm{dist} (pxp, B) < \varepsilon$ for all $x \in \mathfrak F$, and $\| px_1p\| \geq \|x_1\| - \varepsilon$,
        \item $1_A-p \precsim a$ .
    \end{enumerate}
    A non-unital $C^*$-algebra is tracially AF if its minimal unitisation is tracially AF.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
By \cite[Proposition 3.8]{Lin01}, conditions (ii) and (iii) are equivalent to 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*'), start=2]
        \item $pxp \in_\varepsilon B$ for all $x \in \mathfrak F$,
        \item $1-p$ is unitarily equivalent to a projection in $\overline{aAa}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    In fact, the most common definition of simple unital tracially AF algebra in the literature uses condition (ii') rather than (ii).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Every simple, separable, tracially AF \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra has real rank zero, stable rank one and it is also quasidiagonal (\cite[Theorem 3.4]{Lin01}, \cite[Corollary A.22]{FG20}). Additionally, they have strict comparison (as in Definition \ref{def:strictcomp}).
By \cite[Proposition 2.4, Theorem 3.6]{Lin01}, a simple, unital \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra $A$ is tracially AF if and only if for any $\varepsilon > 0$, $\delta > 0$, and any finite subset $\mathfrak F \subset A$, there exists a finite dimensional subalgebra $B \subset A$ with $p=1_F$ such that condition (i), (ii') holds and 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), start=4]
    \item $\tau(1-p) < \delta$ for all normalised quasitraces on $A$.
\end{enumerate}
We will make free use of these properties throughout this section.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $A$ be a unital \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra. A \emph{partition of unity} for $A$ is a finite set $\{p_i\}_{i=1}^n$ of non-zero, mutually orthogonal projections in $A$ which add up to $1_A$.
    
    A \emph{refinement} of $\{p_i\}_{i=1}^n$ is another partition of unity $\{p_{i,j}\mid 1\leq i\leq n, 1\leq j \leq n_i\}$ for $A$ such that $p_i = \sum_{j=1}^{n_i} p_{i,j}$ for all $i$.
head: environment

title: Notation
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Any tuple $(q_k)_k$ of mutually orthogonal projections which is subordinate to a partition of unity $(p_i)_i$, induces a refinement of $\{p_i\}_i$ by adding to $\{q_k\}_k$ the non-zero defects (if there are any) of each $p_i$ by the sum of all $q_k \leq p_i$. We nonetheless introduce the above notion to make notation in some proofs less cumbersome.

    Let $X$ be the Cantor space, and $\tau$ a faithful trace on $C(X)$. Let $p_{1},\dots,p_{n}\in L^{\infty}(X,\mu_\tau)$ be pairwise orthogonal projections and let $\varepsilon>0$. Then there are pairwise orthogonal projections $\tilde{p}_{1},\dots,\tilde{p}_{n}$ in $C(X)$ such that $\lVert p_{i}-\tilde{p}_{i}\rVert_{\tau}\leq\varepsilon$ for each $i$.

label: lemma:inductive-step-v5
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:inductive-step-v5}
    Let $B$ be a unital, simple \ensuremath{C^*}-algebra with a unique trace $\tau$ with strict comparison, containing $C(X)$ unitally with $X$ the Cantor space, such that $\tau$ is diffuse on $C(X)$.
    Suppose that there exist a set $\{e^{(0)}_{ii}\}_{i=1}^{n_{0}}$ of pairwise orthogonal projections of equal trace in $B$ with $e^{(0)}_{11}\in C(X)$, a partition of unity $\{\widetilde e^{(0)}_i\}_{i=1}^{n_{0}}$ for $C(X)$ such that $e^{(0)}_{ii}\leq \widetilde e^{(0)}_{i}$ for all $i$, and $\varepsilon_{0}\geq 4/n_{0}$.
    Then for every $0<\varepsilon_1<1$ and partition of unity $\left\{q_k\right\}_{k=1}^N$ for $C(X)$, there is $n_1\in \mathbb{N}$, a copy of a matrix algebra $M_{n_1}$ in $B$ generated by matrix units $\{e^{(1)}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^{n_1}$ with unit $p_1 = \sum_i e^{(1)}_{ii}$, a partition of unity $\{\widetilde e^{(1)}_i\}_{i=1}^{n_{1}}$ for $C(X)$ refining $\{q_k\}_k$ and a partial isometry $w_1\in B$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(P\arabic*)]
    \item $e_{11}^{(1)}\in C(X)$ and $e_{11}^{(1)}\leq e_{11}^{(0)}$,
    \item $e_{ii}^{(1)}\perp e_{11}^{(0)}$ or $e_{ii}^{(1)}\leq e_{11}^{(0)}$ for each $i$,
    \item $e^{(1)}_{ii}\leq \widetilde e^{(1)}_{i}$ for all $i$,
    \item $w_{1}^{*}w_{1}=1-p_{1}$ and $w_1w_1^{*}\leq p_1$,
    \item $4/n_1 \leq \varepsilon_{1}$,
    \item $\tau(1-p_1)\leq \varepsilon_1$,
    \item $\tau(\mathcal{S}(w_{1}w_{1}^*\mid \{e_{ii}^{(1)}\}))\leq \varepsilon_{1}$,
    \item $\mathcal{I}(p_{0}ap_{0}\mid \{e_{ii}^{(0)}\})\leq \varepsilon_{0}$ for $a\in\{v_1, w_1\}$, with $p_0=\sum_{i=1}^{n_0}e_{ii}^{(0)}$,
    \end{enumerate}
    where $v_1 = \sum_{i=1}^{n_1-1} (e^{(1)}_{i,i+1}+ e^{(1)}_{i+1,i})$.
    If instead of $B$ having strict comparison, we suppose $C(X)$ has dynamical comparison relative to $B$ and $\{e^{(0)}_{ii}\}_{i=1}^{n_{0}}$ is a subset of $C(X)$, then the same properties hold and moreover $\{e_{ii}^{(1)}\}_{i=1}^{n_1}\subset C(X)$.

label: thm:singlegeneration
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:singlegeneration}
    Let $C(X) \subseteq B \subseteq A$ be unital inclusions of unital $C^*$-algebras, with $A$ separable, $B$ simple and with a unique trace $\tau$, which is diffuse on $C(X)$, and $X$ the Cantor space.
    Suppose $B$ has strict comparison or $C(X)$ has dynamical comparison relative to $B$.
    If there is a countable set $\left\{x_n\right\}_n\subset A$ of elements generating $A$ which have small area w.r.t.\ $(C(X),\tau)$, then $A$ is singly generated.

label: cor:amalgams
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:amalgams}
    Let $\{A_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an at most countable family of unital separable \ensuremath{C^*}-algebras with faithful traces, all containing a regular abelian subalgebra $C(X)$ with spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space.
    Suppose that $A_1$ is simple with a unique trace and that $A_1$ either has strict comparison or $C(X)$ has dynamical comparison w.r.t. $A_1$.
    Then the full amalgamated product $A_1*_{C(X)}A_2*_{C(X)}\dots$ is singly generated.
    Consequently, any completion of the algebraic amalgamated free product is singly generated.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:singlegeneration} with $B=A_1$ and Corollary~\ref{cor:smallgenerators} for each of the inclusions $C(X)\subseteq A_i$; note that the unique trace on $A_1$ is diffuse on $C(X)$ by Corollary~\ref{cor:diffuse}.
    Since the full amalgamated product surjects onto any other completion, the result follows.
head: environment

label: cor:sg_tensorprod
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:sg_tensorprod}
    Let $A$ be a $C^*$-algebra satisfying the conditions of Theorem \ref{thm:singlegeneration}. For any unital, separable $C^*$-algebra $D$ and any $C^*$-norm $\alpha$ on the algebraic tensor product $A \odot D$, the $C^*$-algebra $A\otimes_\alpha D$ is singly generated.
